input_text: TITLE: Result of veriﬁcation is not stored reliably SUMMARY: In stellar-core:src/historywork/WriteVerifiedCheckpointHashesWork.cpp 44 =====PAGE 45===== :309, the dir parameter of the fs::durableRename function is speciﬁed incorrectly. The value used is mOutputPath.relative_path().string, while mOutputPath.parent_path().string must be used. The dir parameter of the fs::durableRename function is used to call fsync on the directory containing the ﬁle that is being renamed. This is required to sync the directory metadata, so the renamed ﬁle can actually be discovered. In rare events like power outages or the process being killed, the ﬁle will eﬀectively disappear and the node will have to regenerate it. This variable functions as a lifetime cumulative counter, yet it is directly compared to deposits_cap when evaluating whether a new deposit should be accepted. As a result, the cap check is based on gross historical inﬂows rather than the actual assets currently under management (AUM). This causes the eﬀective cap to drift upward and become overly restrictive, leading the protocol to reject valid deposits even when the actual AUM is well below the intended threshold. 25 =====PAGE 26===== Recommendation We recommend tracking net deposits in order to enforce the desired cap. In some situations, all “yay” votes may be eﬀectively discarded, causing the function to incorrectly return 0% even when “yay” votes exist. For example, if v.YayVotes is 1 and v.TotalVotingPower is 200, the actual percentage should be 0.5%. However, due to integer truncation, the function returns 0%. Consequently, this leads to proposals being incorrectly interpreted as having no support even if “yay” votes are present, causing a critical misrepresentation of voting outcomes. Recommendation We recommend enhancing precision in the aforementioned calculation. input_text: TITLE: Multisig proposals do not expire and cannot be closed SUMMARY: Proposals submitted to the multisig remain in an executable state forever. This could lead to old proposals being executed by a signer after circumstances have changed, for example, when a transaction is not relevant anymore. Additionally, the lack of support for cancelling proposals means that a proposer cannot withdraw a past proposal even if the set of signers changes through a conﬁg change. An example of this being a problem could be a proposal having been replaced by a newer version and then accidentally being executed when the signing threshold is lowered. Recommendation Consider allowing proposers to close proposals and/or adding an expiry time for proposals, after which they cannot be executed anymore. Status: Resolved

input_text: TITLE: Unbounded cache growth allows memory exhaustion attacks SUMMARY: In gnovm/pkg/gnolang/realm.go:80, the pkgIDFromPkgPathCache serves as a shared cache for package paths. While it is initialized with a capacity of 100, this value merely deﬁnes the initial allocation and does not impose an actual limit. Consequently, attackers who can generate arbitrary package paths are able to manipulate the cache size by repeatedly calling PkgIDFromPkgPath with unique package path values. Since no eviction policy exists, the cache will grow indeﬁnitely, leading to excessive memory consumption and potential denial of service issues for nodes. Recommendation We recommend implementing a least recently used or size-based eviction policy to prevent unbounded growth of pkgIDFromPkgPathCache. input_text: TITLE: CFiatV3Wrapper.multiplier has no input validation SUMMARY: In contracts/plugins/assets/compoundv3/CFiatV3Wrapper.sol:39, 52, the rewardMultiplier constructor parameter is stored directly as multiplier in line 52 with no validation. Since this is an immutable value, a mistake cannot be corrected without redeploying the wrapper. input_text: TITLE: Double unlock risk from implicitly copyable lock guards SUMMARY: In src/util/ThreadAnnotations.h:160–163,218–221, the classes MutexLockerT and SharedLockShared each deﬁne a reference data member (MutexType& mut and SharedMutex& mut, respectively). However, they do not declare copy or move constructors or assignment operators. As a result, the compiler implicitly generates these functions, allowing the lock guard objects to be copied. When such RAII lock guards are copied, whether by pass-by-value, return-by-value, or insertion into containers, multiple guard objects reference the same mutex. Both the original and the copy invoke Unlock in their destructors, causing a double-unlock condition that results in undeﬁned behavior. This can manifest as process crashes, memory corruption, or unpredictable data races. The impact is signiﬁcant, as these lock guards are widely used across cryptographic operations, transaction processing, and concurrent data acce [truncated] CODE unknown file: function calls, lambda captures, or container operations remains a realistic risk.

input_text: TITLE: Contracts should implement a two-step ownership transfer SUMMARY: The contracts within the scope of this audit allow the current owner to execute a one-step ownership transfer. While this is common practice, it presents a risk for the ownership of the contract to become lost if the owner transfers ownership to an incorrect address. A two-step ownership transfer will allow the current owner to propose a new owner, and then the account that is proposed as the new owner may call a function that will allow them to claim ownership and actually execute the conﬁg update. Recommendation We recommend implementing a two-step ownership transfer. The ﬂow can be as follows: 1. The current owner proposes a new owner address that is validated and lowercased. 2. The new owner account claims ownership, which applies the conﬁguration changes. The function iterates over all RFQs in the store and checks their expiry status. The issue is that there is no expiry index or pruning mechanism. The function walks every RFQ that has ever been created, so the per-block cost is proportional to the total number of RFQs in the state. After enough RFQ spam, the iteration will exceed the block-time budget, halting consensus. input_text: TITLE: Recalled strategies keep approval and may pull vault assets SUMMARY: In the TezoroV1_1 contract, recallToIdle in src/TezoroV1_1.sol:423-457 sets the target allocation to 0 and freezes deposits, but it does not clear the strategy allowance. The vault grants type(uint256).max approval in addStrategy in src/TezoroV1_1.sol:344-355, and only clears it in removeStrategy in src/TezoroV1_1.sol:358-388. This leaves the external strategy contract inside the vault's token trust boundary even after it is recalled. If the strategy implementation is buggy, malicious, upgradeable, or otherwise compromised, it may still pull idle assets and later deposits from the vault until it is removed. input_text: TITLE: Custom application panics in EndBlocker can halt the chain SUMMARY: Within the x/attestation and x/crosschain modules, custom panics are implemented inthe EndBlocker ifapplication-speciﬁc errors are encountered, which leads the chain to halt. While the SDK itself might intentionally utilize panics as preventive measures against unintended bugs, custom panics within the application's logic in ABCI methods can accidentally introduce vulnerabilities.
